description:
Create an interactive GeoGebra applet demonstrating Archimedes' method of exhaustion for approximating π.

Construct the following in GeoGebra and save as ~/Documents/GeoGebra/projects/archimedes_pi.ggb:

1. A unit circle centered at the origin (0, 0) with radius 1.
2. An integer slider named 'n' controlling the number of polygon sides, ranging from at least 3 to at least 48.
3. A regular inscribed n-gon whose vertices lie on the unit circle, updating dynamically with the slider.
4. A regular circumscribed n-gon whose sides are tangent to the unit circle, also updating dynamically.
5. Numerical display of both π bounds: the inscribed polygon's half-perimeter (lower bound: n·sin(π/n)) and the circumscribed polygon's half-perimeter (upper bound: n·tan(π/n)).
6. At least one text annotation on the Graphics view referencing π and the computed approximation values.

Mathematical reference: At n=6, bounds are [3.0000, 3.4641]. At n=96, bounds are [3.14103, 3.14271]. True π = 3.14159...

Save the completed construction as: ~/Documents/GeoGebra/projects/archimedes_pi.ggb
